results.fact: whether overnight camping at Bird Creek Camp requires a wilderness permit
results.correct_value: Permits are required for overnight stays in the NPS complex (incl. Lake Chelan NRA camps), but Bird Creek Camp is inside the Glacier Peak Wilderness (USFS), where no wilderness permit is needed.
results.evidence: The Park Service states permits are required year-round for overnight stays in the North Cascades NPS complex, including Lake Chelan NRA. The Devore Creek trail enters the Glacier Peak Wilderness about a mile up from the Stehekin River trail, and Bird Creek Camp lies further along, beyond that boundary. The Okanogan-Wenatchee NF says no wilderness permits are required for Glacier Peak Wilderness (visitors sign the register), WTA lists no permit for Devore Creek, and a Flora route page says there is no red tape on this part of the wilderness. So access.permit is right and the blanket "all overnight stays" line in permit is too broad for this trip. (Aside, not patched: WTA notes the Devore Creek trail closed for the Sisi Fire as of 2026-08-27, while access.closures is null.)

results.correct_value: The route leaves Libby Creek Trail at the old cabin (~4.5-5 mi), takes a faint path right into open forest, climbs the boulder field/gully to a pass on the ridge south of the summit, then goes north to the top. It does not go to Libby Lake.
results.evidence: One trip report left the trail at about five miles, went up talus to the pass between Hoodoo Peak and Libby Mountain and up the south ridge, reaching Libby Lake only afterward. A third says to turn right at the old building just before the final hill to the lake, cross boulders to an obvious pass, and find the summit pyramid to the north. None routes via the Libby Lake shore.
